label: GO after an unrewarded a2 -> S2 (common) trial
explanation: Fires only at GO (100% of mass) and only when the previous trial was unrewarded (prev_reward == 0 covers ~100% of activations; never after reward, never at D1/D2). Among those, it is selective for the previous trial having ended in S2 unrewarded: mostly a2 -> S2 common unrewarded (73% of mass), plus a1 -> S2 rare unrewarded (~11%). The remaining ~16% of mass is on the first GO of the window (rel -3), where the previous trial is outside the window and prev variables are unknown, so it cannot be scored; prev_state == 2 & prev_reward == 0 gets recall 0.84 / precision 0.44, and adding rel -3 lifts mass recall to 0.89 at precision 0.49. Recorded the simpler a2-common-unrewarded predicate (dev P 0.69 R 0.72 F1 0.70), all observed variables. This is the model-based switch-away-from-a2 situation; it is not explained by the hidden good state (good == 1 hurts recall) or by the model choice logit. Precision is incomplete: many a2 common unrewarded GO steps are silent, often within long rewarded a2 streaks. Magnitude is small and roughly uniform across the predicate (quartile coverage flat); top examples are at GO after a2 S2c r0 where the agent then chooses a1.
